item.title: 34th for Irishman at Winter Olympics
item.description: Dublin's Cormac Comerford has finished 34th in the men's downhill alpine skiing at the Winter Olympics in Italy. The Olympics debutant clocked a time of just over two-minutes-and-four-seconds, 12 seconds outside the medals. Comerford says it's been an "incredible feeling" to compete at the Games and he's "really proud" of his performance". Advertisement

item.title: Áras an Chontae set to generate 29% of energy on site this year
item.description: The Kerry County buildings are one step closer towards becoming a Net Zero Energy Campus. Áras an Chontae, which uses around 650,000 kWh of electricity every year, will be generating nearly a third of it's energy on site this year. 29% of the required energy for the buildings will be produced from new PV panels. item.title: Celebration of creativity and storytelling by young people in Kerry County Museum
item.description: A new showcase at Kerry County Museum will be a celebration of creativity and storytelling by young people from across the county. The Create + Animate project is part of the Creative Communities initiative, supported by Creative Ireland and Kerry County Council Arts office. The programme has been delivered in schools throughout the county, and involved a series of stop-motion animation workshops open to primary school children. item.title: Rovers sign midfielder on multi-year contract
item.description: Shamrock Rovers have signed midfielder Naj Razi on a "multi-year contract". The 19-year-old returns to Tallaght Stadium after two years at Italian club Como. Hoops boss Stephen Bradley says it was a "no brainer" to bring the Ireland under-19 international back to the club. Advertisement
